items.summary: An open-source (Apache-2.0) chat app where every contact is a real agent — Claude Code, Codex or Grok CLI running on your machine, each with its own model, computer and connected apps. Data stays local and it reuses the subscriptions you already pay for. v0.1.146 shipped Nov 7; it topped GitHub's TypeScript trending list on Nov 11 with about 21,000 stars.
items.title: OpenMausBot: Open-source Grok Bot alternative — every chat contact is a real agent with its own computer (new release Nov 7, GitHub trending)

items.summary: An open-source (MIT) OAuth2 broker written in Go: users grant an agent scoped, revocable access, and the broker holds and exchanges tokens when the agent calls MCP services, so the agent never holds the user's provider credentials. It bridges separate OAuth2 infrastructures, supports delegation chains and keeps audit logs. v0.1 already runs in production inside Zalando, and a Docker Compose tutorial lets you try it locally.
items.title: Agentic Identity Broker: Zalando's open-source identity broker gives agents scoped, revocable access without handing over your tokens (Show HN, Nov 6)

items.summary: A new project from Brian, maker of Xmind: a native Mac app you talk to by holding the right Command key. A front agent handles conversation and memory with almost no tools, while a worker agent — the open-source pi harness — picks jobs from an inbox and runs them inside a sandbox; sending, submitting or deleting anything still needs your confirmation. It runs on your existing ChatGPT or Claude subscription, free to download, and needs macOS 15.4+ on Apple Silicon.
items.title: Nico: A two-agent personal assistant that lives on your Mac — one agent talks, a sandboxed worker does the work (Show HN, Nov 5)
